newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss ease truck limits so some goods evade France. [CORRECTED 17:05 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Swiss ease truck limits so some goods evade France. [CORRECTED 17:05 GMT]

text.p: Switzerland agreed on Thursday to a limited relaxation of its strict size limits on trucks in order to allow loads of perishable goods such as fruit and vegetables to get around France's strike-blocked roads.

But the Federal Office of Police Affairs, in charge of road rules, said it had rejected a request from international transporters for a general lifting of size limits that effectively bar most trans-European trucking.
"We rejected the request, but we are offering limited exceptions for loads of perishable goods if they cannot find space on the truck-trains," spokesman Folco Galli said.

At issue is a Swiss ban on cross-country passage by trucks larger than 28 tonnes, (corrects from 28,000 tonnes) which excludes rigs of 40 tonnes (corrects from 40,000 tonnes) or more most commonly used for trans-European traffic.
A temporary exception had been sought by the International Road Traffic Union (IRU) to allow shipments of three categories of goods to evade road blockades by striking French truckers.
The IRU had asked for permission for bigger trucks to pass through Switzerland if they were carrying perishable goods, animals or supplies crucial to continue production in industry or food making.

But Galli said Switzerland has turned down the request on animal transporters for reasons of disease prevention and added that it was impossible for customs officers at the border to tell which goods were crucial to somebody's production line.
Under the new guidelines, transports over the 28,000-tonne limit with perishable goods must first seek a spot on regular cross-country "piggy-back" trains that carry whole trucks.
If no space was available soon enough, permits would be granted to drive through Switzerland, Galli said.
The new guidelines would be good through December 6 and could be extended if the French trucking strike continues, the spokesman said.

Swiss border crossings have been untouched by strikers in neighbouring France but over 250 blockades on French roads have severly hampered links with Germany and Italy, which also border Switzerland, as well as Britain, Spain and the Benelux countries.
